scope: Read-only archaeological/institutional geography notes for missing profiles cherson, saint-denis, paderborn; no footprint, bbox, or asset reuse authorization

locations.resolvedPlace: Tauric Chersonesos / Chersonesus, ancient city on the Heraclean Peninsula within present-day Sevastopol, southwestern Crimea. This is not modern Kherson city.

publishedReferencePoint.locator: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, component 1411-001 Ancient city of Tauric Chersonese; property 42.8106 ha, buffer 207.22 ha
publishedReferencePoint.note: These are UNESCO's listed point coordinates for the property, not an episode gameplay center or an ancient shoreline coordinate. No conversion or additional coordinate inferred. UNESCO lists State Party Ukraine; its current page records the property as in danger since 2026.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: The ancient city occupies a large promontory between Karantinnaya (Quarantine) and Pesochnaya (Sandy) bays, within Sevastopol.
terrainWaterAccess.consulted: Institutional archaeological portal search result read; direct open failed with HTTP 502.
terrainWaterAccess.limit: Promontory and bays are supported, but this access path does not establish the shoreline or harbor geometry in the 7th century CE.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: Excavated remains include defensive walls/towers, churches, public spaces including a theatre, water reservoir and baths; the town plan is orthogonal, with parallel/perpendicular streets.
terrainWaterAccess.locator: Opening overview, site extent and excavation results
terrainWaterAccess.consulted: Search result read; direct open failed (502). Cross-check: https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1411 overview says orthogonal grid and phases 5th c BCE–13th c CE.
terrainWaterAccess.limit: This is a multi-century urban plan, not proof that every feature or street remained intact/active at Martin I's exile in 655.

locations.episodePeriodCautions: Episode 21 places Martin I's exile/death in 655–656. UNESCO's broad site record spans from Greek foundation in the 5th c BCE through 13th c CE and inventories Greek/Roman/Byzantine/medieval layers. Do not copy Greek-period orthogonal street layout, a generic city wall, a specific harbor, or later medieval/church remains into a 655 scene without phase-specific excavation evidence. Name this place as Cherson/Chersonesos, not Kherson. Modern occupation and jurisdiction of Crimea are politically contested; UNESCO identifies the property with Ukraine and records danger status.
locations.mapsMediaLicensing: UNESCO maps and State Party nomination files are published for transparency/access, but the consulted page provides no blanket reuse license. The archaeological portal includes media and imagery; image credits/license not checked. No maps or images downloaded.

locations.resolvedPlace: Royal abbey/church of Saint-Denis in the historic town of Saint-Denis, north of Paris, Île-de-France, France; not Saint-Denis on Réunion.

publishedReferencePoint.locator: Centre des monuments nationaux press information, visitor access/contact section, printed GPS coordinates for Basilique Saint-Denis
publishedReferencePoint.note: Official visitor-site reference point only; not an excavated medieval perimeter. The French culture heritage record independently identifies the address as 1 rue de la Légion d'Honneur and cadastral parcel 2015 AM 1: https://pop.culture.gouv.fr/notice/merimee/PA00079952.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: The official archaeology portal presents the abbey in relation to the medieval town, its walls, markets, roads/territory interventions and river-based trades of the Croult.
terrainWaterAccess.locator: Sections listed: 'From the royal abbey to the castellum', 'The town within its walls', 'The Croult and river-based trades', 'Archaeological interventions within the town's limits'; interactive map embed 3956
terrainWaterAccess.consulted: Page opened and section labels/map embed inspected; individual map layers and all chapters not opened in this audit.
terrainWaterAccess.limit: These labels establish relevant evidence pathways, not the precise 799 approach road or navigability/riverbank shape at that date.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: Excavation research follows cemetery/burial phases around the basilica; the current basilica sits over an earlier cemetery and the building complex evolved across many centuries.
terrainWaterAccess.locator: Departmental archaeology article, opening paragraphs on preventive excavation and funerary development
terrainWaterAccess.consulted: Institutional page search-result passage read; it describes recent excavation campaign and long chronology.
terrainWaterAccess.limit: Burials and present church footprint do not define a 799 civic map or exact procession route.

locations.episodePeriodCautions: Episode 26 uses Saint-Denis as a local focus in 754, but the historic annalistic claim concerns Stephen's crossing and anointing; no consulted source places the crossing or anointing at Saint-Denis. Episode 31's Paderborn scene is a different geography. The present Gothic basilica's main campaigns are 12th–13th c (French Ministry notice), centuries after 754/799. The archaeology portal's long-term map and town boundaries combine phases; don't transpose modern streets, canal or present abbey complex into the 8th century. The burial/cult origin is a reported tradition and archaeological cemetery site, not proof of all hagiographic details.
locations.mapsMediaLicensing: The Ministry archaeology portal provides an interactive intervention map and credits imagery (e.g. © Monum, © J. Mangin/UASD); no blanket license was seen. Atlas records identify specific image credits, often Department of Seine-Saint-Denis or Musée d'art et d'histoire; those are not public-domain declarations. CMN PDF gives coordinates but no asset reuse license was established. No files downloaded.

locations.resolvedPlace: Paderborn, Westphalia, Germany; episode 31's court/refuge scene refers to Charlemagne's 799 stay at Paderborn, not the 8th-century palace as a fully preserved modern building.

publishedReferencePoint.publishedAddress: LWL-Museum in der Kaiserpfalz, Am Ikenberg, 33098 Paderborn
publishedReferencePoint.locator: LWL museum official contact page, address section
publishedReferencePoint.note: The institutional pages consulted publish an address and a map link but no numeric latitude/longitude. No coordinates inferred or reverse-geocoded for this audit. The named address identifies the museum near the cathedral, not a verified 799 royal-camp point.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: Paderborn occupies a transition between the North German Plain/Westphalian Bight and the Paderborn plateau; the city source describes an abrupt terrain break and upper/lower town, with Pader springs near the cathedral and streams draining toward Pader and Lippe.
terrainWaterAccess.locator: City of Paderborn, 'Allgemeines', paragraphs on natural regions, city-center terrain break, Pader springs and drainage
terrainWaterAccess.consulted: Institutional municipal page opened; searchable text excerpt read.
terrainWaterAccess.limit: Modern broad geomorphology is useful orientation, not 8th-century elevation/land-cover data.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: Karolingian palace remains lie north of the cathedral and were archaeologically found in 1964; a late-8th-century palace is distinguished from a much better-preserved 11th-century Ottonian/Salic palace.
terrainWaterAccess.locator: LWL Museum, museum overview; lines on discovery north of Dom and 8th/11th c phases
terrainWaterAccess.limit: The museum reconstruction is not an 8th-century complete plan. Do not treat the later palace's standing walls/footprint as Charlemagne's court.

terrainWaterAccess.claim: The Pader springs emerge from karstified subsurface of the Paderborn plateau; historical hydrology says the spring basin remained wet/swampy and largely unenclosed until late 12th c, with much settlement above it; the Pader was substantially straightened late medieval to raise water level and aid navigation.
terrainWaterAccess.locator: City waterway page, section 'Historische Entwicklung der Pader' and karst explanation
terrainWaterAccess.consulted: Page opened; groundwater emergence and historical development text checked.
terrainWaterAccess.limit: The medieval and modern channel course is modified; don't copy the modern straightened watercourse or later towpath/navigation into 799.

locations.episodePeriodCautions: For 799, source texts support Charlemagne receiving Leo at Paderborn, but do not pin the meeting to the excavation footprint of the palace or an exact church/courtyard. The municipal visitor account's Karlsburg fortification/town bounds concern 776 and are explicitly based on modern street names; useful only as a source lead, not a ready polygon. The royal palace is late 8th c; distinguish the archaeological palace from the 11th–12th c Ottonian/Salic palace reconstructed as museum. Present-day spring basins, engineered channels, bridge paths and topography include modern interventions. No exact route or water crossing in 799 is established here.
locations.mapsMediaLicensing: LWL and city pages link maps/media and carry photographer/municipal credits; no general reuse license was identified. No map or image downloaded. Numeric coordinates were not supplied by the consulted archaeological/municipal sources, so none are included.

crossLocationLimits: These are place-identification and source notes, not approval of any map footprint, episode boundary, travel route, or gameplay bbox.
Modern map/GPS points mark a current monument or UNESCO property reference, never exact ancient coordinates or a reliable time-slice border.
Search excerpts are labelled as such; direct page consultation failures are stated rather than treated as successful full reading.
